decision.title: Distribution archives: mise, zig cc, seven targets (packet )

body.p: , after , , , . mise run dist builds the sxml command for every supported platform as installable archives (docs/tasks/distribution.md; README.md, "Install").

item.p: Tools: mise.toml pins cmake 3.31.9, ninja 1.13.1, zig 0.15.2, node 22.22.0 and the WASI SDK 34 (github:WebAssembly/wasi-sdk). The tasks are dist, dist:<target>, dist:checksums, dist:verify and install [-- PREFIX] (default ~/.local: bin/sxml, share/doc/sxml/); tools/dist.sh is the one implementation.

Cross-compiling: one toolchain file, cmake/toolchains/zig.cmake, for every native target, chosen by SXML_ZIG_TARGET. Zig carries the C library headers and link stubs for musl, macOS and MinGW-w64, so no sysroot or SDK is downloaded. CMake wants one program per tool and its platform modules rewrite the archiver rules after the toolchain file, so zig cc, zig ar and zig ranlib get two-line shell wrappers in the build tree; the build machine is Linux or macOS. CMake 3.27's --dependency-file link option is turned off (zig's linker rejects it). wasm32-wasi uses cmake/wasi-sdk.cmake with the SDK mise installed. Native builds are Release, wasm32-wasi MinSizeRel (the presets' types), all linked with -s.

Targets: x86_64-linux and aarch64-linux (static musl executables, any distribution), x86_64-macos and aarch64-macos (macOS 11 and later, libSystem only; zig signs the arm64 one ad hoc), x86_64-windows and aarch64-windows (MinGW-w64; only KERNEL32 and the Universal C Runtime, which Windows 10 and later include), wasm32-wasi (the CLI module). Every target builds the library and the CLI with -Werror as they are: no portability fix was needed (the platform layer already had its _WIN32 paths, _getcwd among them).

Archives: sxml-<version>-<target>.tar.gz, .zip for Windows, the version from include/sxml/version.h. Each holds one directory with the program (sxml, sxml.exe, sxml.wasm), LICENSE, README.md and USAGE.md (apps/sxml/README.md, renamed so the two READMEs do not collide). Owners and times are fixed, so the same tree gives the same SHA-256; SHA256SUMS is in sha256sum's format.

Verified here (mise run dist:verify: sxml --version and an sxml xpath query over a small document): x86_64-linux natively, aarch64-linux under qemu-user 8.2, x86_64-windows under wine 9.0, wasm32-wasi under Node.js with tools/run-wasi.mjs. file reports Mach-O x86_64 and arm64 for the macOS programs and PE32+ Aarch64 for aarch64-windows, which nothing here runs.

The owner's machine: running the macOS programs (and aarch64-windows) at all; Developer ID signing and notarization of the macOS programs, as Gatekeeper quarantines an unsigned download (xattr -d com.apple.quarantine works around it); Authenticode signing of the Windows programs if wanted; publishing the archives with a release (docs/RELEASE.md). The macOS programs keep their symbol table (zig's -s does not strip Mach-O; stripping afterwards would break the arm64 signature). The time zones come from /usr/share/zoneinfo (), which Windows does not have.
